items.title: Here is why Madras High Court said house husbands should become the new normal
items.summary: House-husbands should become part of the new normal to preserve the institution of marriage and family, observed the Madras High Court recently while dealing with a matrimonial case. A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi questioned why only women are generally expected to be homemakers, noting that it is a gender neutral term. The Bench added that even the Supreme Court has recognised that the work carried out by homemakers have enourmous economic value. "If there can be house wives, there can be house husbands also. Let this become a new normal. We are of the view that this would help preserve the institution of marriage and family. The expression home maker is gender neutral," the Court observed in its September 23 ruling. Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi Madras High Court If there can be house wives, there can be house husbands also. Let this become a new normal. The expression home maker is gender neutral. The Court noted that, unlike in Western societies, in Indian culture, marriage was historically rooted in family as the core social unit, where the husband was the financial provider and the wife managed domestic duties. items.title: Mumbai court closes Central Library corruption case against Maharashtra minister Chhagan Bhujbal
items.summary: A Mumbai court on Thursday discharged Maharashtra minister Chhagan Bhujbal in the Kalina Central Library scam case [Chhagan Chandrakant Bhujbal v. State of Maharashtra] The order by the special Anti-Corruption Bureau court in Mumbai ends Bhujbal’s trial for alleged corruption and cheating related to the construction project. The prosecution had alleged that Bhujbal misused his official position as the Public Works Department Minister. They claimed he engineered a criminal conspiracy to favor a private developer, India Bulls Real Estate Ltd, by awarding them the library construction contract on a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) basis. Investigators further alleged that Bhujbal received a bribe of ₹2.5 crore through his welfare foundation disguised as corporate sponsorship. Special Judge Mahesh K Jadhav found no sufficient ground to proceed against the senior politician under the Prevention of Corruption Act or the Indian Penal Code. The special judge rejected the prosecution's theory of ‘invisible support’ allegedly provided by the minister to his subordinate officers. items.title: Gujarat court grants bail to journalist Ravi Nair in Adani defamation case
items.summary: A Gujarat court on Thursday granted bail to journalist Ravi Nair in a criminal defamation case filed against him by the Adani Group. Nair, who was convicted in the case earlier this year, was released on bail during the pendency of his appeal, but was again taken into custody on September 17 following the issuance of a non-bailable warrant against him for allegedly not appearing before the appellate court. Principal District and Sessions Judge at Gandhinagar Ashish JS Malhotra today allowed his bail plea. He was represented by Advocate Abhik Chimni. On Wednesday, the Gujarat High Court had r efused to grant him any interim relief on his petition challenging the non-bailable warrant. He had separately moved the sessions court for regular bail. In February, a magistrate convicted Nair in a criminal defamation case filed by the Adani Group in connection with a series of tweets and online articles accusing the conglomerate of numerous unethical practices. The Court ruled that the content went beyond fair criticism and amounted to criminal defamation. Adani Group had filed a criminal complaint in September 2021. items.title: Heggana Muddu review: Small moments shine in this relationship drama from Avinash Belekkala
items.summary: Heggana Muddu (Kannada) Writer-director Avinash Belekkala of Heggana Muddu (loosely translated as Cute Bandicoot) can write the small moments that other writers struggle with really well. The silences, the understanding looks, the face as a tapestry of emotions … they all land perfectly. A film about a young couple pushed into marriage after a meeting and numerous mundane, bordering on boring, text messages provides plenty of opportunities for these small moments. But first a word about the performances. Ajitha might be written as a red flag, but what a glorious red flag Poornachandra Mysuru makes. Over the years, it has become clear that he is an actor who is criminally underutilised in an industry that is struggling to find and retain a new generation of actors. As for Aditi Sagar, what does one even say! Her face is like a transparent shield between the world and her, showcasing every doubt, joy, sadness, or question. She’s also someone who acts with her physique. Over the course of the movie, she goes from someone confident to vulnerable, before discovering herself. And, she gets you to understand all of this without uttering a word. Heggana Muddu begins very promisingly as a r

items.title: Supreme Court refuses to halt forensic audit of Fortis transactions in Daiichi-Singh brothers dispute
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to interfere with a Delhi High Court order directing a forensic audit of Fortis Healthcare in connection with the Daiichi Sankyo-Singh brothers dispute [ Fortis Vs Daiichi Sankyo]. However, a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified that the High Court's observations against Fortis were only tentative and prima facie and would not bind the forensic auditor. The forensic audit will have to be conducted independently without being influenced by those observations. “It goes without saying that the forensic audit shall be conducted independently without being influenced by those observations made by the High Court, ” the Court added. The proceedings arose out of Daiichi Sankyo's efforts to enforce a 2016 arbitral award against the Singh brothers and other judgment debtors. The dispute subsequently expanded to examine what happened to the Singh brothers' substantial shareholding in Fortis while proceedings were pending before courts. According to the submissions before the Supreme Court, the Singh brothers earlier controlled around 70 percent of Fortis. Their shareholding subsequently fell sharply

items.title: GEM Veeramani case: SIT investigation ordered; detailed ground report | Shabbir Ahmed | TNM Tamil
items.summary: The renewed investigation in the Veeramani POCSO case eventually led to his arrest. According to the police, the case was formally registered only in October 2025, after a pen drive containing a video showing a minor being sexually assaulted was handed over to the Anti-Vice Squad by a child rights NGO. However, in February 2026, the police filed a report seeking to drop further action, citing difficulties including identifying the girl in the video. But the NGO says it repeatedly followed up with the police after reporting the incident, but was told that the complaint was “in process”. In this week's episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed speaks to AJ Hariharan, the NGO's secretary about its role in reporting the alleged abuse, its follow-up with police and what it witnessed during the renewed probe.

items.title: 5 officers suspended, 543 properties demolished, 178 sealed after Satya Niketan PG collapse: MCD to Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) told the Delhi High Court on Friday that after the recent collapse of a paying guest (PG) building in Satya Niketan, it has demolished 543 properties, sealed 178 and slapped 354 show-cause notices for unauthorised construction. In an affidavit filed before the Court, the MCD stated that action was also taken against its officials as well. The Court was informed that five officers in the supervisory chain have been placed under suspension. "The senior-most officers connected with the concerned zonal and building administration were also placed under suspension, including the Deputy Commissioner of the concerned Zone and the Superintending Engineer / South Zone, being the senior-most officer in the building hierarchy at the relevant level, along with the Executive Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Junior Engineer concerned," the MCD stated. The MCD also stated that there are 2,453 PGs operating in the national capital with 32,247 rooms, housing 50,529 people. items.title: Kerala High Court bans unauthorised photography, videography in its premises; issues guidelines
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has notified guidelines to regulate photography, video recording, and live streaming on its premises. Named the ' General Guidelines for the regulation of Photography, Videography and Live Streaming in the High Court premises ', these guidelines are aimed at ensuring security, privacy, decorum, and smooth operations at the High Court. The guidelines prohibit photography, videography and live streaming within High Court premises except when permitted under separate guidelines regarding the allotment of certain premises within the High Court such as the auditorium and banquet hall, for special events. An exception may be also carved out with the prior permission of the Registrar General or anyone authorised to do the same by the Chief Justice. The guidelines also ban uploading, publishing, circulating, and disseminating photos, videos, or live streams recorded within High Court premises on social media and other electronic media without prior permission from the Registrar General or an authorised person. items.title: CIC advises Centre to restart publishing paper-wise marks of candidates who clear UPSC exam
items.summary: The Central Information Commission (CIC) has advised the Central government to reinstate the practice of publishing paper-wise marks of candidates who clear the Civil Services Examination (CSE). Information Commissioner Jaya Varma Sinha noted that the subject-wise marks of successful candidates were made public till 2018 but were discontinued without any policy decision on record. The Commission said that publishing these details was in the interest of transparency and building faith in the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), a constitutional body. “An advisory under Section 25 (5) of the RTI Act is issued to the Respondent Public Authority DoPT to reinstate the practice of publication of detailed break-up marks obtained by recommended candidates in Civil Services (Mains) Examination. This advisory by the Commission to reinstate this practice is based on the reliance (and the fact) that the same was done prior 2018 and was discontinued without any policy decision on record,” the Commission said in its September 24 decision. items.title: Delhi High Court halts London arbitration in UN military cargo dispute
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has issued an injunction restraining arbitration proceedings in London in connection with a dispute over the transportation of military cargo for the United Nations Peacekeeping Force (UNPKF) to Sudan [SARR freights Vs Agro Coal] A Division Bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Renu Bhatnagar found that the final transportation contract between SARR Freights and Argo Coral Maritime did not contain an arbitration clause. The Court said that an arbitration clause appearing in earlier negotiations could not be read into an agreement signed later, especially when it expressly superseded previous arrangements. "An anti-arbitration injunction is accordingly granted restraining the defendant/respondent, Argo Coral Maritime Ltd., from continuing, pursuing or taking any steps in the LMAA arbitration titled 'Argo Coral Maritime Ltd. v. SARR Freights Ltd/SARR Freights Corporation'," the Court directed. items.title: Supreme Court asks BCI to consider withdrawing upper age limit for 5-year LL.B
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Bar Council of India (BCI) to consider withdrawing the upper age limit prescribed for admission to five-year integrated LL.B [Rishabh Duggal & Anr. v. Bar Council of India & Anr.] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a challenge to the BCI's prescription of the upper age limit. Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain , appearing for the petitioner, argued that the BCI's power to prescribe minimum qualifications under the Advocates Act could not be extended to impose an upper age limit. “The power to impose minimum qualifications, can it ever be converted into an upper age limit? This power itself is missing under the Advocates Act,” contended Hossain. The BCI, however, said the upper age limit was prescribed because most five-year law courses were residential. “We have imposed the upper limit because most of the five-year law courses are residential. items.title: Missing train ticket cannot defeat compensation claim after passenger’s death: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday held that a missing train ticket could not, by itself, defeat a compensation claim by the parents of a man who died after falling from the train [Sukhabhai Nanjibhai Makwana and Another v. Union of India] A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar set aside a Gujarat High Court ruling that had rejected the parents’ compensation claim after finding insufficient evidence that their son had fallen from a train. “ On preponderance of probabilities, it can be concluded that the victim was a bona fide passenger and that absence of recovery of his ticket cannot result in defeating the claim for compensation, ” the Court said. The Bench thus restored the ₹8 lakh compensation awarded by the Railway Claims Tribunal and directed the Railways to satisfy the award within 30 days. Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar The case arose from the death of Maheshbhai, who fell from a train between Sabarmati and Ahmedabad railway stations on September 27, 2017. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday reserved its verdict on a plea filed by the Shahi Jama Masjid Committee at Sambhal challenging a trial court order directing the appointment of an Advocate Commissioner to survey the mosque's premises [ Committee Management, Jami Masjid Sambhal v. Hari Shankar Jain & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe reserved its decision on the plea challenging the Allahabad High Court's May 2025 decision to uphold the trial court's ex-parte order allowing the survey of the mosque's premises. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The trial court had passed its November 2024 directive in a suit involving allegations that the mosque was constructed over a demolished Hindu temple during the Mughal era. The suit was filed by advocate Hari Shankar Jain and seven others. The civil court order allowing the survey had led to violent clashes in Sambhal. The dispute concerns an interview given by Priya to online media outlet Can Channel. Hassan claims that the interview included sexually coloured remarks against her, which were intended to outrage her modesty and damage her reputation. She asserted that Priya's comments and the online circulation of such content, amounted to the commission of a cognisable criminal offence. Hassan initially approached the Palarivattom Police seeking action. After the police refused to register an FIR, she approached judicial magistrate first class court in Ernakulam for relief. However, on July 27, the magistrate court dismissed her plea for registration of an FIR, relying on a police report which stated that the allegations did not disclose a cognisable offence and that Hassan could pursue a private complaint for defamation. items.title: Supreme Court seeks NIA response to bail plea of man accused of links to Dawood Ibrahim’s gang
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday issued notice on a bail plea filed by a man accused of helping the gang led by terrorist Dawood Ibrahim extort money and move funds through hawala routes [ Shabbir Abubakar Shaikh v. National Investigation Agency ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta sought the National Investigation Agency’s (NIA) response to a plea filed by Shabbir Abubakar Shaikh challenging a Bombay High Court order that refused him bail. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The NIA alleges that Shaikh acted on instructions from Dawood Ibrahim and Chhota Shakeel and helped extort ₹16 crores from a protected witness between 2008 and 2018. It also claims he received ₹25 lakhs through hawala routes in April 2022, kept ₹5 lakhs and passed the remaining ₹20 lakhs to another accused. The agency alleges that the money was intended for terrorist and criminal activities. Shaikh disputes his alleged links to the gang and denies that the money was meant for terrorism. He has also challenged the application of the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999 (MCOCA) to his case. A special NIA court rejected his bail plea in December 2024. items.title: Kerala High Court flags poor facilities in POCSO courts after judges visit; asks State to act
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently raised concerns over inadequate facilities in courts dealing with cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act [District Bar Association & anr v State of Kerala & ors] A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM visited the courts only to find that most of them did not confirm to the prescribed guidelines under the POCSO Act. On September 23, the Court directed the state government to take immediate steps to bring such courts in line with POCSO guidelines. " During the visit to the District Courts, we found that most of the POCSO courts do not conform to the guidelines specified under the POCSO Act. The facilities are also inadequate, " the Court observed. Therefore, it directed the State government to take immediate steps to bring such courts in line with POCSO guidelines. The Bench also directed the Registrar (District Judiciary) to file an affidavit specifying the number of additional courts required to deal with POCSO cases in Kerala.
